description: Issue #985: neutralizes FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard.BuildMap's new principal-key check (compile-preserving operator: `&& false` appended to the throw condition, never a deletion) so BuildMap can no longer reject a FileAttachment-principal FK whose relationship targets a non-canonical, Guid-typed principal key (a Guid alternate key, single or composite). Without this check, such an FK is treated as an ordinary Guid candidate and resolved by DCExtension.ResolveFileAttachmentIds's hardcoded `x.ID` query -- the exact defect #985 fixes. red_test is the CONCRETE false-allow reproduction from the issue: a victim FileAttachment (ID=V, AlternateGuid985=A, TENANT_VICTIM) and an attacker's own FileAttachment (ID=A -- deliberately equal to the victim's AlternateGuid985 -- TENANT_ATTACKER) both exist; the attacker's dependent FK carries A (the TRUE relationship, via AlternateGuid985, points at the VICTIM's row). With the check neutralized, the guard's `x.ID == A` query, scoped to TENANT_ATTACKER, matches the ATTACKER'S OWN row and incorrectly reports the reference resolved -- SaveChanges succeeds SILENTLY instead of throwing NotSupportedException. green_test is Test 4 (the positive control from the same file): an in-tree, convention-discovered, canonical FileAttachment.ID-keyed FK (ProductWithOptionalPhoto.PhotoId, declared in FkWriteGateSeventhRoundSqliteTests815.cs, exercised via BypassGuardContext824 -- a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT DbContext type/model/test fixture from the mutated GuidAlternateKeyContext985/GuidAlternateKeySeedContext985 pair the red test uses) still saves normally -- proving this mutation's blast radius is scoped to the non-canonical-principal-key shape and does not collaterally break the one FK shape every in-tree model actually uses. Decoupling: the green test's own model has ZERO non-canonical-principal-key FKs anywhere, so IsCanonicalFileAttachmentPrincipalKey short-circuits `true` for its only FileAttachment FK and the mutated `&& false` term is never even evaluated on that code path -- the green test exercises BuildMap's per-property Guid-typed-candidate loop (unchanged by both the fix and this mutant), not the mutated condition itself.
target_symbol: FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard.BuildMap -- the #985 principal-key rejection condition, line ~338-339

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.VM.FileAttachm: Assert\.ThrowsException failed\. Expected exception type:<System\.NotSupportedException> but no exception was thrown\.

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first, Release build, dotnet build test/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.csproj -c Release) with the mutant patch applied manually (git apply, then git apply -R to revert -- run before this entry's target file was committed, so run_mutant.py's own clean-tree gate was bypassed only for this one-off capture, never for the recorded gate verdict below): 'Assert.ThrowsException failed. Expected exception type:<System.NotSupportedException> but no exception was thrown. #985: BuildMap must reject this model shape before any resolution query runs -- this is what makes the false-allow collision above unreachable.' The 'but no exception was thrown' phrasing (not 'Actual exception type:<...>') is itself the false-allow signature: SaveChanges completed successfully under the mutant, i.e. the attacker's forged reference was silently permitted, which is the specific defect this mutant proves the #985 check prevents -- distinct from the false-reject signature ('Actual exception type:<...UnresolvableFileAttachmentReferenceException>') that Test 1's own RED-before-fix run produced against the SAME production defect with different (non-colliding) test data. Re-run via run_mutant.py itself after the fix was committed (see production-readiness.md's #985 row for the KILLED/GATE:PASS confirmation and determinism check).
